bibl.title: Exceptional damage-tolerance of a medium-entropy alloy CrCoNi at cryogenic temperatures

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the equiatomic three-element CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy, and its strength, ductility and fracture toughness from room temperature to 77 K
span.quote: Here we examine an equiatomic medium-entropy alloy containing only three elements, CrCoNi, as a single-phase face-centred cubic solid solution, which displays strength-toughness properties that exceed those of all high-entropy alloys and most multi-phase alloys.

span.label: whether the properties of these alloys come from high configurational entropy itself or from which elements are present
span.quote: Although this excellent combination of properties can be related to progressively increasing strain hardening with hardening exponents above 0.4 (refs), it remains unclear why this particular combination of elements with very different crystal structures produces a single-phase microstructure, whereas many others with comparable configurational entropies do not.

span.label: a three-element alloy whose damage tolerance exceeds every high-entropy alloy reported, and the argument that element identity matters more than element count
span.quote: With respect to high-entropy alloys in general, by comparing the CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi alloys, the current work does lend credence to our belief that it is the nature of elements in complex solid solutions that is more important than their mere number.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Significantly, we find here that the fracture toughness properties of the three-component CrCoNi MEA are even better than those of the five-component CrMnFeCoNi HEA, and are further enhanced with decrease in temperature between 293 and 77 K, making it one of the toughest metallic materials reported to date.

span.label: simultaneous increase of strength, ductility and toughness as temperature falls, against the usual strength-toughness compromise
span.quote: Although in most materials the achievement of strength and toughness is invariably a compromise—high strength is often associated with lower toughness and vice versa—it has become increasingly apparent that the presence of twinning as the dominant deformation mechanism serves to ‘defeat this conflict', specifically by providing a steady source of strain hardening, which promotes ductility by delaying the onset of plastic instability by necking, and an additional deformation mode besides dislocation plasticity to accommodate the imposed strain.

span.label: uniaxial tension and fracture-toughness testing from 293 to 77 K, with SEM of the propagated crack and X-ray diffraction to confirm the single phase
span.term: uniaxial tension and fracture-toughness testing from 293 to 77 K, with SEM of the propagated crack and X-ray diffraction to confirm the single phase
span.quote: To seek the origins of such strength, ductility and fracture resistance between 293 and 77 K, we conducted detailed SEM analysis of the vicinity of the propagated crack; this was performed on samples sliced in two through the thickness to ensure that deformation conditions had been in fully plane strain (Fig. 3a).

span.label: the three-element alloy twins at room temperature where the five-element one deforms by slip alone, and the extra deformation mode arrives before the strength penalty does
span.quote: We did not observe deformation nano-twinning at room temperature in the five-component alloy, where deformation at 293 K is solely carried by dislocation slip, specifically, involving the rapid movement of partial dislocations and the much slower planar slip of undissociated dislocations, although as with the present three-component alloy, twinning became a major deformation mode at 77 K. We believe that the earlier onset of deformation nano-twinning is key to the exceptional damage-tolerance of this medium-entropy alloy.

span.label: twinning supplies steady strain hardening, which delays plastic instability by necking, and adds a second way to accommodate strain besides dislocation motion
span.quote: Although in most materials the achievement of strength and toughness is invariably a compromise—high strength is often associated with lower toughness and vice versa—it has become increasingly apparent that the presence of twinning as the dominant deformation mechanism serves to ‘defeat this conflict', specifically by providing a steady source of strain hardening, which promotes ductility by delaying the onset of plastic instability by necking, and an additional deformation mode besides dislocation plasticity to accommodate the imposed strain.

span.label: why this particular combination of elements forms a single phase while others of comparable configurational entropy do not remains unexplained
span.quote: Although this excellent combination of properties can be related to progressively increasing strain hardening with hardening exponents above 0.4 (refs), it remains unclear why this particular combination of elements with very different crystal structures produces a single-phase microstructure, whereas many others with comparable configurational entropies do not.

span.label: the dislocation glide mechanism is presumed from the five-element alloy rather than observed directly in this one
span.quote: Similarly, back-scattered electron (BSE) scans taken on specimens fractured at room (Fig. 3b) and cryogenic temperatures (Fig. 3d) show the formation of pronounced dislocation cell structures akin to the five-component CrMnFeCoNi HEA where dislocation motion is associated with glide of ½<110> dislocations on {111} planes, a typical deformation mechanism for fcc materials, which we presume also occurs in our three-component CrCoNi MEA.

span.label: the twinning-induced plasticity mechanism, recognised first in Hadfield manganese steels and copper thin films and applied here to explain an entropy-named alloy
span.quote: In addition to the high- and medium-entropy alloys, there are now several other materials known to benefit from twinning, including copper thin films and 11–15 wt.% (Hadfield) Mn-steels (used in the mining industry for rock crushers because of their hardness and fracture resistance) and their modern variant known as twinning-induced plasticity steels, which have application in the automobile industry.

span.label: the five-element CrMnFeCoNi alloy, tested by the same group over the same temperature range, as the comparison
span.note: eliminates: a cryogenic toughness attributed to medium-entropy composition when the five-element alloy from the same laboratory over the same range is the thing it must beat · outcome: held
span.quote: Such damage-tolerant properties of the CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy are literally unprecedented for mechanical behaviour at cryogenic temperatures. For a material with a tensile strength of 1.3 GPa to display ductilities (failure strains) of 90%, and ‘valid' crack-growth fracture toughnesses that exceeds 430 MPa m1/2, all at liquid-nitrogen temperatures, is exceptional and clearly exceed the excellent cryogenic properties of our previously reported CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy.

span.label: that the specimens were in fully plane strain, checked by slicing through the thickness
span.note: eliminates: a fracture toughness inflated by a specimen that was not in plane strain, which the standard requires and which thickness alone does not guarantee · outcome: held
span.quote: To seek the origins of such strength, ductility and fracture resistance between 293 and 77 K, we conducted detailed SEM analysis of the vicinity of the propagated crack; this was performed on samples sliced in two through the thickness to ensure that deformation conditions had been in fully plane strain (Fig. 3a).

span.label: that the alloy is genuinely single-phase, checked by XRD, backscattered electron imaging and the ternary phase diagram
span.note: eliminates: a second phase supplying the strength that is being attributed to the single-phase solid solution · outcome: held
span.quote: The experimental results (X-ray diffraction and backscattered electron, BSE, images) are consistent with the CrCoNi ternary phase diagrams, which indicate that the equiatomic composition is a single-phase solid solution at elevated temperatures.

span.label: single-phase character at the atomic scale, checked by three-dimensional atom probe tomography - on the FIVE-element alloy, not this one
span.note: eliminates: fine-scale segregation hidden below the resolution of diffraction - established by atom probe tomography for the FIVE-component alloy, and not for this one · outcome: absent-stated-about-other
span.quote: In addition, three-dimensional atom probe tomography on the five-component CrMnFeCoNi alloy in the cast/homogenized state and after severe plastic deformation have shown that it retains its true single-phase character at the much finer atomic scale.

span.label: High-entropy alloys
span.quote: High-entropy alloys are an intriguing new class of metallic materials that derive their properties from being multi-element systems that can crystallize as a single phase, despite containing high concentrations of five or more elements with different crystal structures.

span.label: medium-entropy alloy
span.quote: Here we examine an equiatomic medium-entropy alloy containing only three elements, CrCoNi, as a single-phase face-centred cubic solid solution, which displays strength-toughness properties that exceed those of all high-entropy alloys and most multi-phase alloys.

span.label: configurational entropy
span.quote: In fact, a relatively small number of the reported multi-element high-entropy alloys are simple solid solutions. Cantor et al. produced an alloy with 20 elements in equal atomic ratios that crystallized as a very brittle multi-phase microstructure indicating that high configurational entropy by itself is unable to suppress the formation of intermetallic phases comprising the constituent elements.

span.label: Cantor alloy
span.quote: CrMnFeCoNi (often termed the Cantor alloy) displays strongly temperature-dependent strength and ductility with only a small strain-rate dependence. Furthermore, between room temperature and 77 K, the alloy displays fracture toughness, KJIc,values at crack initiation that remain well above 200 MPa m1/2 associated with an increase in tensile strength (763→1,280 MPa) and ductility (0.5→0.7), making it not simply an ideal material for cryogenic applications but putting it among the most damage-tolerant materials in that temperature range.

span.label: nano-twinning
span.quote: We did not observe deformation nano-twinning at room temperature in the five-component alloy, where deformation at 293 K is solely carried by dislocation slip, specifically, involving the rapid movement of partial dislocations and the much slower planar slip of undissociated dislocations, although as with the present three-component alloy, twinning became a major deformation mode at 77 K. We believe that the earlier onset of deformation nano-twinning is key to the exceptional damage-tolerance of this medium-entropy alloy.

span.label: strain hardening
span.quote: Such properties appear to result from continuous steady strain hardening, which acts to suppress plastic instability, resulting from pronounced dislocation activity and deformation-induced nano-twinning.

span.label: solid solution
span.quote: The experimental results (X-ray diffraction and backscattered electron, BSE, images) are consistent with the CrCoNi ternary phase diagrams, which indicate that the equiatomic composition is a single-phase solid solution at elevated temperatures.

span.label: intermetallic phases
span.quote: In fact, a relatively small number of the reported multi-element high-entropy alloys are simple solid solutions. Cantor et al. produced an alloy with 20 elements in equal atomic ratios that crystallized as a very brittle multi-phase microstructure indicating that high configurational entropy by itself is unable to suppress the formation of intermetallic phases comprising the constituent elements.

span.label: twinning-induced plasticity steels
span.quote: In addition to the high- and medium-entropy alloys, there are now several other materials known to benefit from twinning, including copper thin films and 11–15 wt.% (Hadfield) Mn-steels (used in the mining industry for rock crushers because of their hardness and fracture resistance) and their modern variant known as twinning-induced plasticity steels, which have application in the automobile industry.

span.label: 'high-entropy alloy' = FIVE OR MORE elements at high concentration, crystallising as a single phase
span.quote: High-entropy alloys are an intriguing new class of metallic materials that derive their properties from being multi-element systems that can crystallize as a single phase, despite containing high concentrations of five or more elements with different crystal structures.

span.label: 'medium-entropy alloy' = the same thing with THREE - the two categories differ by an element count and nothing else
span.quote: Here we examine an equiatomic medium-entropy alloy containing only three elements, CrCoNi, as a single-phase face-centred cubic solid solution, which displays strength-toughness properties that exceed those of all high-entropy alloys and most multi-phase alloys.

span.label: the same class is called high-entropy alloys, multi-component alloys OR compositionally complex alloys - three names, one referent
span.quote: Equiatomic multi-component metallic materials, referred to variously as high-entropy alloys (HEAs), multi-component alloys or compositionally complex alloys, have generated considerable excitement in the materials science community of late as a new class of materials that derive their properties not from a single dominant constituent, such as iron in steels, but rather from multiple principal elements with the potential for unique combinations of mechanical properties compared with conventional alloys.

span.label: high configurational entropy BY ITSELF does not suppress intermetallics - a twenty-element equiatomic alloy came out brittle and multi-phase
span.quote: In fact, a relatively small number of the reported multi-element high-entropy alloys are simple solid solutions. Cantor et al. produced an alloy with 20 elements in equal atomic ratios that crystallized as a very brittle multi-phase microstructure indicating that high configurational entropy by itself is unable to suppress the formation of intermetallic phases comprising the constituent elements.

span.label: equiatomic composition maximises configurational entropy and does NOT minimise Gibbs free energy - the two come apart
span.quote: As pointed out recently, while the equiatomic composition maximizes configurational entropy, it does not necessarily minimize the total Gibbs free energy of a multi-component solid solution, and increasing the number of constituent elements could actually lead to the formation of undesirable intermetallic phases.

span.label: contradicts → the premise that maximised configurational entropy is what stabilises a single-phase multi-element solid solution
span.note: the corpus holds gild2016, which rests on that premise. This paper supplies the counterexample - a twenty-element equiatomic alloy that came out brittle and multi-phase - and concludes for element identity over element count
span.quote: In fact, a relatively small number of the reported multi-element high-entropy alloys are simple solid solutions. Cantor et al. produced an alloy with 20 elements in equal atomic ratios that crystallized as a very brittle multi-phase microstructure indicating that high configurational entropy by itself is unable to suppress the formation of intermetallic phases comprising the constituent elements.

span.label: extends → the CrMnFeCoNi Cantor alloy and its reported cryogenic damage tolerance
span.note: same group, same tests, two elements removed - and the smaller alloy wins
span.quote: CrMnFeCoNi (often termed the Cantor alloy) displays strongly temperature-dependent strength and ductility with only a small strain-rate dependence. Furthermore, between room temperature and 77 K, the alloy displays fracture toughness, KJIc,values at crack initiation that remain well above 200 MPa m1/2 associated with an increase in tensile strength (763→1,280 MPa) and ductility (0.5→0.7), making it not simply an ideal material for cryogenic applications but putting it among the most damage-tolerant materials in that temperature range.

span.label: qualifies → the belief that useful new alloys lie near the centres rather than the corners of phase diagrams
span.quote: Much of the interest is predicated on the belief that many new alloys with useful properties are likely to be discovered near the centres (as opposed to the corners) of phase diagrams in compositionally complex systems.

span.label: medium-entropy alloy —distinct-from→ High-entropy alloys
span.note: differs in: the number of principal elements - three against five or more, with no other criterion separating them · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: Here we examine an equiatomic medium-entropy alloy containing only three elements, CrCoNi, as a single-phase face-centred cubic solid solution, which displays strength-toughness properties that exceed those of all high-entropy alloys and most multi-phase alloys.

span.label: configurational entropy —causes→ intermetallic phases
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.85 — asserted as the field's premise and then denied - high entropy 'by itself is unable to suppress' them
span.quote: In fact, a relatively small number of the reported multi-element high-entropy alloys are simple solid solutions. Cantor et al. produced an alloy with 20 elements in equal atomic ratios that crystallized as a very brittle multi-phase microstructure indicating that high configurational entropy by itself is unable to suppress the formation of intermetallic phases comprising the constituent elements.

span.label: nano-twinning —causes→ strain hardening
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: Such properties appear to result from continuous steady strain hardening, which acts to suppress plastic instability, resulting from pronounced dislocation activity and deformation-induced nano-twinning.

span.label: twinning-induced plasticity steels —contrasted-with→ nano-twinning
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — a different materials class reaching the same benefit by the same mechanism, which is why the mechanism is not specific to entropy
span.quote: In addition to the high- and medium-entropy alloys, there are now several other materials known to benefit from twinning, including copper thin films and 11–15 wt.% (Hadfield) Mn-steels (used in the mining industry for rock crushers because of their hardness and fracture resistance) and their modern variant known as twinning-induced plasticity steels, which have application in the automobile industry.

span.label: the three-element alloy has better fracture toughness than the five-element one, and improves as temperature falls
span.quote: Significantly, we find here that the fracture toughness properties of the three-component CrCoNi MEA are even better than those of the five-component CrMnFeCoNi HEA, and are further enhanced with decrease in temperature between 293 and 77 K, making it one of the toughest metallic materials reported to date.

span.label: nano-twinning begins at room temperature in the three-element alloy and only at 77 K in the five-element one
span.quote: We did not observe deformation nano-twinning at room temperature in the five-component alloy, where deformation at 293 K is solely carried by dislocation slip, specifically, involving the rapid movement of partial dislocations and the much slower planar slip of undissociated dislocations, although as with the present three-component alloy, twinning became a major deformation mode at 77 K. We believe that the earlier onset of deformation nano-twinning is key to the exceptional damage-tolerance of this medium-entropy alloy.

span.label: high configurational entropy alone does not suppress intermetallic formation
span.quote: In fact, a relatively small number of the reported multi-element high-entropy alloys are simple solid solutions. Cantor et al. produced an alloy with 20 elements in equal atomic ratios that crystallized as a very brittle multi-phase microstructure indicating that high configurational entropy by itself is unable to suppress the formation of intermetallic phases comprising the constituent elements.

span.label: it is one of the toughest materials in any materials class ever reported
span.quote: Indeed, in terms of (valid) crack-initiation and crack-growth toughnesses, the CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy represents one of the toughest materials in any materials class ever reported.

span.label: High-entropy alloys
span.quote: High-entropy alloys are an intriguing new class of metallic materials that derive their properties from being multi-element systems that can crystallize as a single phase, despite containing high concentrations of five or more elements with different crystal structures.

span.label: medium-entropy alloy
span.quote: Here we examine an equiatomic medium-entropy alloy containing only three elements, CrCoNi, as a single-phase face-centred cubic solid solution, which displays strength-toughness properties that exceed those of all high-entropy alloys and most multi-phase alloys.

span.label: room temperature: tensile strength near 1 GPa, failure strain about 70%, KJIc above 200 MPa m1/2 — None
span.quote: At room temperature, the alloy shows tensile strengths of almost 1 GPa, failure strains of ∼70% and KJIc fracture-toughness values above 200 MPa m1/2; at cryogenic temperatures strength, ductility and toughness of the CrCoNi alloy improve to strength levels above 1.3 GPa, failure strains up to 90% and KJIc values of 275 MPa m1/2.

span.label: at cryogenic temperature: above 1.3 GPa, failure strain up to 90%, KJIc 275 MPa m1/2 — None
span.quote: At room temperature, the alloy shows tensile strengths of almost 1 GPa, failure strains of ∼70% and KJIc fracture-toughness values above 200 MPa m1/2; at cryogenic temperatures strength, ductility and toughness of the CrCoNi alloy improve to strength levels above 1.3 GPa, failure strains up to 90% and KJIc values of 275 MPa m1/2.

span.label: crack-growth toughness exceeding 430 MPa m1/2 at liquid-nitrogen temperature — None
span.quote: Such damage-tolerant properties of the CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy are literally unprecedented for mechanical behaviour at cryogenic temperatures. For a material with a tensile strength of 1.3 GPa to display ductilities (failure strains) of 90%, and ‘valid' crack-growth fracture toughnesses that exceeds 430 MPa m1/2, all at liquid-nitrogen temperatures, is exceptional and clearly exceed the excellent cryogenic properties of our previously reported CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy.

span.label: twenty elements in equal atomic ratios produced a brittle multi-phase microstructure — None
span.quote: In fact, a relatively small number of the reported multi-element high-entropy alloys are simple solid solutions. Cantor et al. produced an alloy with 20 elements in equal atomic ratios that crystallized as a very brittle multi-phase microstructure indicating that high configurational entropy by itself is unable to suppress the formation of intermetallic phases comprising the constituent elements.

span.label: the Cantor alloy: tensile strength 763 to 1,280 MPa and ductility 0.5 to 0.7 between room temperature and 77 K — None
span.quote: CrMnFeCoNi (often termed the Cantor alloy) displays strongly temperature-dependent strength and ductility with only a small strain-rate dependence. Furthermore, between room temperature and 77 K, the alloy displays fracture toughness, KJIc,values at crack initiation that remain well above 200 MPa m1/2 associated with an increase in tensile strength (763→1,280 MPa) and ductility (0.5→0.7), making it not simply an ideal material for cryogenic applications but putting it among the most damage-tolerant materials in that temperature range.

span.label: strain-hardening exponents of the order of 0.4 — None
span.quote: Although this excellent combination of properties can be related to progressively increasing strain hardening with hardening exponents above 0.4 (refs), it remains unclear why this particular combination of elements with very different crystal structures produces a single-phase microstructure, whereas many others with comparable configurational entropies do not.

span.label: strain-hardening exponent
span.quote: Although this excellent combination of properties can be related to progressively increasing strain hardening with hardening exponents above 0.4 (refs), it remains unclear why this particular combination of elements with very different crystal structures produces a single-phase microstructure, whereas many others with comparable configurational entropies do not.

span.label: fracture toughness
span.quote: Significantly, we find here that the fracture toughness properties of the three-component CrCoNi MEA are even better than those of the five-component CrMnFeCoNi HEA, and are further enhanced with decrease in temperature between 293 and 77 K, making it one of the toughest metallic materials reported to date.

span.label: configurational entropy
span.quote: As pointed out recently, while the equiatomic composition maximizes configurational entropy, it does not necessarily minimize the total Gibbs free energy of a multi-component solid solution, and increasing the number of constituent elements could actually lead to the formation of undesirable intermetallic phases.
